correction: An earlier reading called SAC converged to a grasp-only local optimum after lift went 0.08 -> 0.00 at 276k steps. That was PREMATURE: it was a plateau, not convergence.

why_it_is_real.breadth: 10 of 25 conditions improved by >1.0 return, each with genuine lift (0.026-0.128 m); only 2 regressed
why_it_is_real.not_an_outlier: unlike the single 138k success, this is a distributed shift -- mean displacement 0.0111 -> 0.0881 m
why_it_is_real.one_full_success: condition 22 reached return 35.557 with 0.35 m displacement

training_vs_eval_gap.observation: training blocks show 0-1 lifts per 20 episodes while deterministic eval shows 40%
training_vs_eval_gap.explanation: training samples stochastically at the learned entropy; evaluation uses the deterministic mean. Lifting needs a sustained precise grasp across 23 chunks, and injected noise at every chunk usually drops the piston. The deterministic policy HAS learned to lift; the behaviour policy mostly cannot execute it.
training_vs_eval_gap.prediction: as alpha continues annealing, training-time lifts should begin to appear

lesson: do not call a plateau a local optimum; late-stage skills emerged between 276k and 414k steps
